### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**5** anchor(s) derived from **3** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 76bff41f451d3fa3d475384d8483905f49f6607f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c2e588a2fe257a2a2ef5cd29b057291c1d61e855` — the merge of head `3945fcf5332f9511b6c1d21cd19b128020cbf431` into base `76bff41f451d3fa3d475384d8483905f49f6607f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c2e588a2fe257a2a2ef5cd29b057291c1d61e855 && git checkout c2e588a2fe257a2a2ef5cd29b057291c1d61e855
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 76bff41f451d3fa3d475384d8483905f49f6607f 3945fcf5332f9511b6c1d21cd19b128020cbf431 && git checkout -B drift-repro 76bff41f451d3fa3d475384d8483905f49f6607f && git merge --no-ff 3945fcf5332f9511b6c1d21cd19b128020cbf431

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 76bff41f451d3fa3d475384d8483905f49f6607f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `22261181b09bdcab1d75c3fc4297f15b40d00269`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/formula/src/index.ts, packages/formula/src/relationship-traversal.ts, packages/formula/src/validate-hop-list-equality-36237.test.ts, packages/formula/src/validate.ts, packages/lint/src/authored-site-expression.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.hop-list-equality-36237.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts + read, not reviewed: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.cel-list-equality-refused.ts (main), packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts (`resolveTraversalScope`), packages/objectql/src/engine-master-detail-related.ts (`resolvePredicateRelated`, `resolveOneHopRelated`), packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts (the formula hop binding), packages/lint/src/authored-site-expression.ts, skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md (main), .changeset/36237-hop-list-equality.md (for ② only)

Inputs read: card #36237 body and all 8 comments (triage, claim, two amendments, three dev reports, one progress note; no earlier contract record on the thread); PR #36673 body and its 9-file list; the net diff `origin/main...22261181`; the check-runs on the head (57 success, 11 skipped, 0 failure; Check Changeset, Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core 10/10, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard and Dogfood Regression Gate all success).

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set, narrowed — right.** At a validation rule's `condition` / `when` (nested branches included) and at a field `expression`, `==` / `!=` between a one-hop read `record.REF.LEAF` and a non-null string, number or boolean literal is now an error when REF is a single-valued reference whose target, as served, declares LEAF list-valued. Read against the engine: both sites hydrate through one loader (`resolveOneHopRelated`, read by `find`), a rule with an empty or multi-valued reference is refused before evaluation (`resolveTraversalScope`, `no-reference`), so where the predicate is evaluated at all the read is the stored list or `null` and the comparison is a constant. No per-row answer is taken away.
- **Accept-set, what stays accepted — right, each traced in the code.** A scalar leaf; `== null` / `!= null` (`scalarLiteralOf` refuses `null`); `in`; a non-literal operand; a reference that is itself multi-valued (`ownLists.includes(field)`, matching the loader's own "names no single row"); a target outside the index, tied between two packages, or in the stored-metadata family; a second hop (`hopMemberOf` answers only the exact one-hop node); a `record` a comprehension macro binds; a `previous` hop (never hydrated, so not judged); every site that serves no hop (`traversalHydration` unset). Each of these is a missed catch at worst, never a false refusal.
- **Root case unchanged — right.** `forEachListEquality` is the old walk of `checkListEquality` with `errors.push` replaced by a callback; the comprehension handling, the two-sided loop and its `break` are the unchanged lines of the hunk. The root `subjectOf`, the flattened-site gate and `filterCompiled` stay in `checkListEquality`. A hop read is not a root read (`rootMemberOf` on `record.account.labels` sees a non-id receiver), so no comparison is reported twice.
- **Public surface, widened — right as declared.** `findHopListEquality(source, listLeaves)` is a new root export of `@objectstack/formula`; `hopMemberOf` is exported from its module and not from the package entry. `ExprSchemaHint` is unchanged. The export is the card's route 2 and keeps the refusal's words, params and rewrite in one place (`listEqualityRefusal`), which a lint-side copy would have forked.
- **Doors — right, narrower than the root case.** `os validate` / `os build` and the object save door refuse it (the lint test pins `runtimeWriteType: 'object'`); the MCP tool's gate half carries it too, since `judgeAuthoredSiteExpression` runs `runStackExpressionPasses` and the SITE_CALLS ledger now classifies the pass at both sites. The shared-validator half and the Studio draft check do not see a hop. The card's Done-when admits this through its second arm (told at save).

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` are right, and the PR body and the changeset body carry the same pair. `yes`: a new export reached by the built entry. `(narrowing)`: a value an author could save is refused. `narrowed` outranks anything else the diff does; no metadata key, value or type is added.
- `@objectstack/formula: minor` and `@objectstack/lint: minor` match: a protocol kind takes at least minor on each package the diff moves, and neither is graded patch. The BREAKING banner, the FROM / TO pair and the one-line fix are in the changeset body. Check Changeset is green on the head.
- The ADR-0087 marker `not-required (already-registered cel-list-equality-refused)` passes the gate, but its written reason does not hold against the entry it names: see S1.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in all three dev reports. Nothing to answer.
- Flag, lap 1: the four ledger rows were outside the file surface. Answered by claim amendment 1; the rows are in the diff and are ledger rows only (two `pass` rows with a `HOP_LIST` fixture, one `pass-silent-here` row, three PLUMBING receivers). Test Core is green on the head.
- Flag, lap 2: the export cannot leave the public entry without a second copy of the refusal. Answered by claim amendment 2 and confirmed in the tree: the pieces the refusal is built from are module-private in `validate.ts`.
- Flag, deviation: tests were cited at earlier heads. Answered by the check-runs on this head; laps 2 to 3 changed only the changeset.
- Out-of-scope finding 1 (the ADR-0087 entry's surface prose does not name a hop read; `carrier: none`): not accepted as out of scope. It is S1.
- Out-of-scope finding 2 (the validator half of `validate_expression` and the Studio draft check do not see a hop; `carrier: none`): accepted under the card's Done-when, and escalated to the seat as N1, since a finding with no carrier is lost at merge.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The diff issues no query, materialises no id set and joins nothing in the app; the pass reads the lint's existing in-memory indexes.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing does not take a declared capability away. Nothing on `main` declares that a list reached through a hop can be compared with a scalar: the spec's own entry says the comparison answers one constant, the skill teaches the refusal and the membership rewrite, and the engine serves the hop as the stored list. The prescribed rewrite was traced where it is prescribed: at a rule the hydrated row always exists when the predicate runs, and the loader materialises a declared column the driver omitted as `null`, so `has()`, the `!= null` guard and `in` all answer; the lint test shows the rewrite itself saves clean. What the diff does not do is make the spec's refusal real as the spec states it, because the spec's statement stops short of a hop.

S1 (should-fix) — the registered breaking change does not describe what this PR refuses. `cel-list-equality-refused` (packages/spec, on `main`) bounds its `surface` to a read of a list-valued field "on `record` / `previous`", and its `replacement` says `os validate`, `os build`, the MCP `validate_expression` tool and the Studio object editor's draft check refuse the shape. After this PR a third read, `record.REF.LEAF` at a validation rule and a field `expression`, is refused under the same code, and for that read the Studio draft check and the validator half of the tool do not refuse. The changeset's marker says the entry "now covers the hop read too"; only its acceptance command does, mechanically. The entry is the published record an upgrader reads to learn what a BREAKING minor refuses, and it now under-states the surface and over-states the doors for the new part. Fix: extend the entry's `surface` to the one-hop read at the two hop-serving sites and state the doors for it, in this PR or in a PR this one names as landing with it; or have the seat rule in writing that the entry stays as it is, with a card carrying the amendment. The dev saw the gap and left it with no carrier.

N1 (nit) — door parity has no carrier. The Studio draft check and the validator half of `validate_expression` judge list equality through `ExprSchemaHint` only, so an author in Studio is told at save and not while typing. This is inside the card's Done-when. File a follow-up card (the card's route 1, a hint member for hop targets' list-valued fields, is the natural shape); no change on this head.

N2 (nit) — `refuseHopListEquality` builds its reference map, walking every served object and every field of the hopping object, before it knows the source holds a comparison or a hop. Its sibling `refuseUndeclaredHopField` returns first when the source traverses nothing. The verdict is the same either way; the cost is paid once per rule predicate and per field expression. Left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up; a fix here moves the head.

N3 (nit) — the PR body's "Acceptance notes" and "Readings" still describe lap 1 (a known red on four ledger rows, files outside the surface). The tree and the check-runs say otherwise. Prose face; correct the body.

Tried and held: a false refusal through a non-reference field named like a reference (`referenceTargetOf` is undefined, no map entry); a self-reference (the target index is the object's own); double reporting with the root pass; a bound `record` inside a macro; the bracket spellings; an unmapped or multi-hop read; a source that does not compile (left to `invalid-cel`).

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-36237-hop-list-equality`
Reviewed-by: `session_011y7As6YDLR8TJVDpdXzJyV`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 — REWORK · head 22261181b09bdcab1d75c3fc4297f15b40d00269 · card #36237

L2 record at this head: comment 7112500193 (PASS, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, narrowing face, one open should-fix S1) · 2026-11-23T20:04Z. I read it against GitHub (`git diff origin/main...22261181`, `l1-face.mjs --pr 36673`, `pr-state.mjs`), not against the report.

### Checklist
- Shape: open, draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #36237`. No closing keyword binds another card.
- Code: `forEachListEquality` is a mechanical extraction, and the root case is unchanged. `findHopListEquality` judges `record.REF.LEAF` reads only where `REF` is single-valued, and `refuseHopListEquality` runs at the two hop-serving sites (rule predicate under `traversalHydration`, formula `expression`). Both packages are published, and both have a changeset entry.
- Declarations: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` in the PR body and the changeset. `yes` is right because the new root export `findHopListEquality` widens `@objectstack/formula`. Level `minor` on both packages is right for `narrowed`.
- `Skills-docs:` line present and true: the `objectstack-formula` skill already teaches the list-equality refusal and the `has()`-guarded `in` rewrite.
- Dogfood battery in full at this head (report 7112286256): `22261181` · VERDICT command-exit 0 · 487 files passed, 3 skipped · 4121 tests passed, 68 skipped · no failures.
- Gates at this head: 57 success, 11 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending. Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check are success.

### REWORK items
1. **S1 (L2, should-fix): the ADR-0087 entry this PR cites does not describe what it refuses.** `cel-list-equality-refused` bounds its `surface` to a read "on `record` / `previous`". Its `replacement` says the MCP `validate_expression` tool and the Studio draft check refuse the shape, but neither refuses the one-hop read this PR adds. The marker's reason ("that entry's acceptance check … now covers the hop read too") does not make the entry true. Take one of two routes:
   - (a) In this PR, extend the entry's `surface` to the one-hop read `record.REF.LEAF` at a validation rule's predicate and a field `expression`, and state its doors (`os validate` / `os build` / the object save door; not the Studio draft check or the tool's validator half). Regenerate the artefacts `packages/spec` owes (AGENTS.md § *Touched `packages/spec`*). This adds the schema face to the L2 delta.
   - (b) The seat rules in writing on #36237 that the entry stays as it is, and files a card that carries the amendment. The marker's reason then names that card instead of claiming coverage.
   Route (a) is the default: the entry is what an upgrader reads to learn what this BREAKING `minor` refuses.
2. **PR body (L2 N3).** `## Acceptance notes` still opens with "KNOWN RED … 4 tests in `@objectstack/lint` fail", and `Readings` is at `ff7e133d` / `72a1bda7`. At this head the two ledger files are in the diff (`d26a320b`) and CI is green. Rewrite both for the final head.
3. **`!` (nit, prose).** The title and the changeset headline read `fix(lint):`. Most `(narrowing)` changesets on main carry `!` (23 of the 30 sampled), and #36676 and #36683 carry it. Add it to both while the changeset is open for item 1.

### Owed after the fix
- A contract review delta at the new head, by the same reviewer, closing S1 by id.
- The dogfood battery again only if route (a) moves code outside `.changeset/` and the PR body. A `packages/spec` entry edit counts as moving code.

### Out of scope, disposition
- L2 N1 (the Studio draft check and the validator half of `validate_expression` do not see a hop, so a Studio author is told at save, not while typing): the seat files a card, or folds it into the route (b) card.
- L2 N2 (`refuseHopListEquality` builds its map before checking that the source holds a comparison): accepted, no correctness effect.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a59d4a847b86a08a2050a908a78b41e9e0f148b7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.cel-list-equality-refused.ts, packages/formula/src/index.ts, packages/formula/src/relationship-traversal.ts, packages/formula/src/validate-hop-list-equality-36237.test.ts, packages/formula/src/validate.ts, packages/lint/src/authored-site-expression.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.hop-list-equality-36237.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts + read, not reviewed: packages/lint/src/authored-site-expression.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts (`resolveTraversalScope`), packages/objectql/src/engine-master-detail-related.ts (`resolveOneHopRelated`), .changeset/36237-hop-list-equality.md (for ② only)
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

Delta review of the record on head `22261181` (comment 7112500193, PASS with S1 open). The head moved by one commit, `a59d4a84`, touching two files: the changeset and the ADR-0087 semantic entry `cel-list-equality-refused`. No path under packages/formula or packages/lint changed between the two heads, so every judgment of the earlier record on those eight files stands and is not repeated. The diff now touches `packages/spec/src`, so the schema face is added to the narrowing face; the floor is all nine code paths.

Inputs read: the delta diff `22261181..a59d4a84` and the net file list against `main` (10 files); the refreshed PR title and body; dev report 7122909194 on card #36237; the check-runs on `a59d4a84` (0 failure; Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Lint & Repo Gates, Spec property liveness, TypeScript Type Check, Build Core, Test Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard and Dogfood Regression Gate all success).

S1: closed
N3: closed

### ① Derived judgments

- **The entry's `surface`, extended — right against the code.** It now names the one-hop read `record.REF.LEAF` at a validation rule's `condition` / `when` (nested branches included) and a field `expression`, REF a single-valued reference and LEAF a list-valued field of its target, compared with the same literals. Each clause is what the tree does: the two call sites of `refuseHopListEquality` (the rule helper under `traversalHydration`, and the field-expression judge), `ownLists.includes(field)` for the single-valued reference, and `scalarLiteralOf` for the literals. Its four exclusions (a multi-valued reference, a second hop, a `previous` hop, a hop at any other site) are each a branch read in the earlier round.
- **The entry's `replacement`, extended — right against the code.** The rewrite it prints for the hop read is `listMembershipRewrite`'s CEL spelling on the hop reference. The doors it states are the real ones: `os validate`, `os build` and the object save door refuse (the lint test pins `runtimeWriteType: 'object'`); the Studio draft check and the shared-validator half of the MCP `validate_expression` tool do not, because `ExprSchemaHint` carries the root object's fields only. The sentence about the root shape's doors is unchanged and still true of the root shape.
- **No accept-set or public-surface change in the delta.** The entry edit is prose in two string fields; no schema shape, key or export moves. `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria` are untouched, and the acceptance command (`os validate` or `os build`, no `list-equality` finding) covers the hop read through the same code.
- **Generated artefacts — consistent, by the check-runs.** Lint & Repo Gates, Spec property liveness, Build Core and TypeScript Type Check are green on the head; the entry's text has no generated copy in the tree at this head.

### ② Semver level

- `'@objectstack/spec': minor` is right: the diff now moves the spec package, and a `narrowed` protocol kind takes at least minor on every package the diff moves. `@objectstack/formula` and `@objectstack/lint` stay minor. Check Changeset is green on the head.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` are unchanged and identical in the PR body and the changeset body. The title and the changeset headline now carry `!`, matching the BREAKING line.
- The ADR-0087 marker `not-required (already-registered cel-list-equality-refused)` now gives a reason that holds: this change extends that entry's surface to the one-hop read and states its doors, which is what the entry edit does. The earlier reason, that the entry already covered the hop, is gone.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in report 7122909194. Nothing to answer.
- Flag, deviation: two derived gates exited 3 locally on a first run and 0 on a re-run. Answered by the check-runs on this head, which are the gate verdicts.
- Out-of-scope finding (the Studio draft check and the shared-validator half of `validate_expression` do not see a hop; `carrier: none`): answered. It is now a stated limit of the published entry and of the changeset, and it is inside the card's Done-when. A carrier is still owed if the limit is to be lifted; it stays N1.
- The earlier out-of-scope finding on the entry's surface prose is closed by this commit (S1).
- SQL push-down: no finding. The delta is prose and a changeset.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing now makes the spec's own refusal real. The published entry states the hop read as part of the refused surface, bounds it to the two sites the engine hydrates, and says which doors refuse it and which do not; the lint enforces exactly that. Nothing a spec on `main` declared as a capability is taken away, as judged on the earlier head.

Read against its first consumer: an upgrader who reads the entry learns that `record.account.labels == 'vip'` at a validation rule or a field expression is refused, gets the rewrite the refusal itself prints, and is told the refusal arrives at build and at save, not in the Studio draft check.
